message: please don't sign off on any open container waiver. we already have people drinking on stoops and in the park every weekend and the noise and broken bottles are bad enough as it is.

I live on East 9th between 1st and 2nd and just saw that a weed shop called Bellanova wants to open at number 331. There are already a few of these within a couple blocks. How many do we need? I'd like the board to look hard at this one.

I run a small shop in the East Village and my landlord has stopped doing repairs and keeps hinting I should leave before my lease is up. There's supposedly a law against this but nobody enforces it and I can't afford a lawyer. Can the city put someone in charge of tracking this and helping businesses like mine?

Our neighbors are scared to go to the clinic or drop their kids at school because they don't know if local police will hand them over to ICE. I hope the board backs the New York for All Act in Albany so state and city officers stay out of federal immigration enforcement.

Saw the plans for a wheelchair lift out front of 4 St. Marks Place. I want the building to be accessible, but it's an 1830s townhouse, so please make sure moving the fire escape and changing the balcony doesn't wreck the front of it.
The middle of Allen Street has been a sad strip of concrete for years. I'm all for turning part of it into real parkland, as long as it doesn't change what can be built along the street.

I'm 71 and on a fixed income, and every year my out of pocket costs go up. Please support the New York Health Act. Single payer would mean nobody around here has to choose between rent and seeing a doctor.

so many people locked up have mental illness or addiction and jail just makes it worse. would love to see the board get behind expanding treatment courts so judges can send people to treatment instead of a cell.

Composting in East River Park was a neighborhood institution before the park got torn up. Really glad to see a new compost yard and learning center planned down by the Corlears Hook ferry stop. Hope it opens soon and local schools can use it.

Harold Hunter grew up skating in this neighborhood and inspired a whole generation of kids. Naming the field in the northeast corner of Tompkins Square after him would mean a lot to the skate community.
Term limits for district managers sounds like a way to let politicians push out the people who actually know how the neighborhood works. I'm against Intro 501 and hope the board says so.

Bar Belly at 14B Orchard wants seating out in the street again. Orchard is already jammed on weekend nights and those sheds bring the noise right up to our windows. Please think about the people living upstairs.

My family has lived on East 10th near Avenue D for decades and we all knew Kavion. Putting his name on the block between Avenue D and the FDR would help people remember him. A lot of us in the buildings signed the petition.

Essex Market is supposed to serve the people who live here, not just tourists. Whatever changes they make to how it's run, I want cheap vendors, free events, and programs for low-income families to stay.

Hi, I volunteer with a group that looks after Sara D. Roosevelt Park. The sandbox at Hester Street Playground is full of trash and rats and parents just avoid it. We're asking for support to swap it out for synthetic turf that kids can actually play on.
It would be wonderful to see East 2nd St between B and C carry the names of Marsha P. Johnson and Sylvia Rivera. They fought for so many people and deserve to be remembered on our streets.
strongly support naming that skate field after harold hunter. kids still skate there every day.

I own Fire Escape, the dispensary at 103 Avenue A. We'd like to add a walk-up window so people can pick up orders without crowding inside, same hours as now, with staff watching the line. Hoping the board will back us.
Another cannabis store, this time at 5 Division St? That stretch by the Manhattan Bridge has lots of seniors and families. I'd like to know who's running it and how they'll handle security.

Intercity buses loading in front of 9 Chatham Square is a terrible idea. Traffic between Doyers and Mott is already a mess and the sidewalk is narrow. Where are all those passengers and suitcases supposed to go?

Children's Magical Garden has been a free place for neighborhood kids for over 40 years. My daughter would be thrilled with a tree house and a little stage for shows, and the new fence and sidewalk are long overdue. Please support the improvements!

With all the ICE raids and hate going around, people on the Lower East Side need to look out for each other. I'd love to see the board join the LES Community Care Coalition and help spread the know-your-rights trainings.
cien fuegos at 95 ave a wants a roadway shed. fine by me as long as it's kept clean and they close it up at a decent hour.
Brownie Morales did so much for the Lower East Side for so many years. Please support putting her name up at the corner of Stanton and Eldridge. Everyone around here knew her.
Is Commodore opening a second place at 14 Avenue C? That part of Avenue C is mostly apartments and I'm worried about late night crowds. I'd like to hear their hours before anything gets approved.
Soothr on East 13th is a great restaurant but their sidewalk tables already make it hard to get by with a stroller. If they're adding more outdoor seating at 204, please keep a clear path.
I'm the owner of Binondo, a small cafe. We're moving from Canal Street to 50 East Broadway and need to bring our beer and wine license with us. Same quiet cafe, same hours, just a new address.

Love the idea of a neon art piece on the new Barrier Free Living building at 270 East 2nd. Housing for domestic violence survivors with disabilities is exactly what we need, and a hopeful message out front is a nice touch.

Why is someone who barely shows up still on the board? I've heard Alistair Economakis has missed a huge number of meetings. The rest of the members give up their evenings, so he should too or step aside.
please make sure the new bathroom building in the park actually gets built and stays open. right now families and runners have nowhere to go.

There's a liquor license application for 110 Forsyth St, two storefronts combined. Forsyth already has several bars and on weekends it's loud until 4am. Please look at their hours and soundproofing before saying yes.

It's not fair that the city only gets 20 percent back from the state for public health work when other counties get more. Please support raising it to 36 percent so the health department can keep clinics and outreach going.

Spicy Moon on the Bowery is asking for sidewalk seating. I walk past 265 Bowery every day and it's already tight with deliveries and people waiting for tables, so please make sure there's room left to walk.

Seven cameras on the Cooper Union Foundation Building? It's one of the most important landmarks we have. I get the security concern, but they should be small and tucked away, not bolted all over the front on East 7th.
Delivery trucks double park on our block of East 12th all day, especially near 520. A loading zone would really help. Right now cars can barely get by and the sidewalk is full of boxes.
My son learned to skate at Tompkins because of guys like Harold Hunter. Calling the field there 'Harold Hunter Court' just feels right.

I'm a parent at a District 1 public school and some of my kid's classmates have stopped coming because their families are afraid of ICE. Please back the parents' council push to keep immigration agents out of our schools.

I manage a restaurant on Clinton between Stanton and Rivington. Our box truck deliveries have nowhere to stop, so the drivers end up blocking the whole street. Can the loading zone be made longer so the trucks fit?

The hotel at 154 Madison wants to turn two parking spots in front into a loading zone. Parking around Pike and Madison is already hard to find for residents. Not sure the hotel needs it more than we do.
Who's running the 4th of July party on Eldridge between Houston and Stanton? A daytime BBQ is fine, but please put a firm end time on the music.
Treasure Club at 22 Orchard wants a roadway cafe. Lower Orchard already has tons of outdoor setups and garbage piles up around them. I'm against adding another one.
I live on East 6th between A and B. A new whiskey bar called Caledonia at 511 is applying for a full liquor license. The block already has a few bars, so I'd want limited hours and no tables outside.

When the city picks a new group to run Essex Market, please make sure it's a local organization that actually knows the Lower East Side. The kitchen and mezzanine upstairs should be for neighborhood events and classes, not private parties.

Carlota at 14A Orchard Street just applied for a license. That's right next to Bar Belly, so the block would turn even more into a nightlife strip. Please hear from people who live on Orchard before deciding.
it would be great to have little signs naming the plants along the waterfront parks. my kids always ask what everything is and a lot of it is native.
I run on the East River Park track after work and in winter it's pitch dark by 5. Please push for real lights on the track as part of the park rebuild. It's the only proper track downtown.
The bar on my corner wants to take out its second bar and put in a pool table. Honestly sounds like an improvement, more of a neighborhood hangout. No objection from me.

Please keep Jefferson Street between East Broadway and Henry as an open street this year. Kids from the buildings around there use it to ride bikes and play. I hope St Marks and Orchard get good hours too.

I organize with delivery workers in Chinatown and the LES. Workers have nowhere to park their e-bikes or rest, so they end up on the sidewalk and police take bikes worth thousands of dollars. We're asking the board to support bike parking and rest spots where the restaurants are busiest.
I'm a senior on a pension and would love to ride Citi Bike, but the cost adds up. A cheaper rate for older riders would get a lot of us out and moving.
Ping at 22 Mott is applying for beer and wine. It's a restaurant in the middle of Chinatown, seems reasonable to me as long as it stays a restaurant and doesn't turn into a bar.
Closing Mott Street from Canal to Bayard every Saturday from July to December? I own a small store on that block and our deliveries need to get in. Half a year of Saturdays is a lot.
The walkway south of the Rivington playground in Sara D. Roosevelt Park could really use benches and some shade. Parents waiting on their kids have nowhere to sit. Glad Parks is redesigning it.

I'm torn about the 21-story building planned at St. Augustine's on Madison Street. We badly need 130 affordable apartments, but it's a lot taller than what's around it. Please make sure the old chapel really gets restored.
Bellevue is where my whole family goes, insurance or not. With Medicaid cuts coming out of Washington, I hope the board pushes the city and state to protect its funding.

If St. Mark's Church on East 10th is selling air rights for the project on Third Ave, I want to know the money actually goes into fixing up the church. It's the oldest place of worship in Manhattan and it needs the work.
Letting council members pick community board members would turn the boards into political clubs. I'm opposed to Intro 322 and hope you are too.

What did the hospital's neighborhood health survey find? Living near Chinatown I see lots of seniors with diabetes and nowhere close to get help. I'd like NewYork-Presbyterian Lower Manhattan to share the results with the community.
for the district budget requests this year please prioritize senior centers and affordable housing. rents are pushing out people who've lived here forever.
Every year I hear about budget priorities but nothing seems to change. Please ask the city for more trash pickups, school repairs and mental health outreach in our district.
I'm one of the owners of the dispensary planned at 68 Clinton Street. We're local, we'll close by 9 most nights and we've hired security. We'd really appreciate the board's support.

The old church at 121 East 7th is being turned into apartments with extra floors on top. Please make sure they keep the stained glass and the original windows on the front. That's what makes the building special.
There's a new cafe/bar on my block applying for beer and wine, room for about 74 people. That's big for a quiet side street. I'm worried about noise late at night.
Since the fire, the lot where Middle Collegiate stood at 112 Second Avenue has just been fenced off. A garden there would be a beautiful way to honor the church while they figure out what's next.
The Market Line at Essex Crossing was supposed to be small vendors and local food, not a Burlington. Please fight the big box store at 115 Delancey.
Freedom For Ukraine at 136 Second Ave applied for a liquor license. I support them, it's a nice spot and they've been good neighbors.
Salvatore and Eric Dellecave deserve to be remembered. I support co-naming Pike Street between Henry and Madison in their honor.
My kids are at ABC Playground on Houston and Essex almost every day and it's falling apart. So happy it's being rebuilt. Please make sure there's shade and working bathrooms.
I went to the board office for a meeting and it's cramped and run down. If the city won't let the board move, at least fix the place up so staff and the public can use it properly.
please support the senior discount for bike share. lots of us older folks would ride if it were cheaper
Jackdaw at 213 2nd Ave wants sidewalk tables. It's a good bar but I'd want the tables cleared at a reasonable hour.
When you send the city our list of needs, please include real money for public housing repairs. Leaking roofs and broken elevators have gone on for years.
We're organizing the Chinatown block party on Forsyth between Canal and Division on July 24, with food, music and activities for families. We'd love the board's support!
The Halloween dog parade is the best day of the year! Hope it gets approved again for October 18.
The Church of St. Mary on Grand Street is one of the oldest Catholic churches in the city and it still isn't landmarked. Please support protecting it before someone tries to tear it down.
the sandbox at the playground is gross and the kids can't use it. please support fixing it.
The market has lost a lot of its affordable stalls lately. Before the city signs a new deal with whoever runs it, ask them to commit to local vendors and community programs.

I'm glad DOT wants to make Avenue B safer along Tompkins Square, but switching it to one-way between 7th and 10th worries me. Will traffic just get pushed onto the side streets? I do like the bike lane and safer crossings by the schools.

I heard Lower Eastside Service Center plans to renovate 46 East Broadway and move a state addiction services office in. The building needs work, but how will they manage people coming and going on that busy stretch?

Turning Captain Jacob Joseph Playground at Henry and Rutgers into a dog run feels wrong. The city let that playground fill up with trash and drug use for years. Fix it for the kids who live here first.
EVLovesNYC has been handing out free groceries to our neighbors every week since the pandemic. They deserve the board's backing, and maybe help finding more space.
This neighborhood has always been home to immigrants. Please stand up for keeping New York a sanctuary city. People need to feel safe calling 911 or sending their kids to school.
St. Nicholas of Myra on East 10th has those cheap vinyl windows that are falling apart. Aluminum ones closer to the originals would be a big improvement for the church.
